answer: Agents must present a dual-channel identity interlock, checked like a safety-rated guard: a wharf-side hardware root of trust signs each action, and a mirror copy of that attestation must match before any transaction clears. An attacker must forge both channels per identity, so each fake agent costs a physical secure element plus a valid signed attestation, not just a keypair. The ivory limit: compromised hardware batches can clone roots, so remote attestation alone never reaches full integrity.
